summary: General Terms and Conditions of the TRAVEL health insurance for foreign travel, issued by DKV Luxembourg S.A. Cover applies to a temporary stay abroad specified in the insurance application, for a minimum of seven days and a maximum of fifty-six days, and reimburses medically necessary outpatient, hospital and dental treatment plus additional services and repatriation, up to a maximum total of EUR 150,000 per person and per insured stay. Eligibility is restricted to existing customers of one of the three companies of the LALUX Group who reside in Luxembourg or a neighbouring country and are affiliated to a compulsory statutory health insurance scheme. The premium is charged per day of cover: EUR 2.00 per person per day up to age 69, EUR 8.00 from age 70.

definitions.definition: Any natural person who is already a customer of at least one of the three companies of the LALUX Group (LA LUXEMBOURGEOISE Société Anonyme d'Assurances, LA LUXEMBOURGEOISE-VIE Société Anonyme d'Assurances or DKV Luxembourg S.A.), resides in Luxembourg or one of the neighbouring countries and is affiliated to the compulsory health insurance scheme in Luxembourg or to an equivalent statutory health insurance scheme (e. g. Joint Sickness Insurance Scheme (JSIS) of the European Union).

a) Any natural person who meets the conditions of a policyholder within the meaning of Article 1.1, or; b) Any close relative of a natural person who meets the conditions of a policyholder within the meaning of Article 1.1., provided that the said close relative is usually resident in geographical Europe and is affiliated to a compulsory statutory health insurance scheme or an equivalent health insurance scheme. The following are considered to be close relatives of the policyholder: spouse, partner under a civil union contract (e. g. Civil Solidarity Pact), biological children, adopted children, children with no biological relation to the policyholder or children placed with the policyholder by virtue of a court order, aged under twenty-six (26) years, or aged over twenty-six (26) years provided that they are under guardianship or supervision.
Any insured person who suffers an insured event.

An insured event is an unforeseeable accident or illness suffered by the insured person during their stay abroad, justifying benefits in favour of the latter, as set out in Article 11. In the event of the occurrence of an insured event, our intervention will cease as soon as a medical diagnosis concludes that benefits of a medical nature are no longer necessary. All benefits of a medical nature that are not linked to the original insured event are considered to result from a new insured event.

Gross negligence includes: failure to comply with the instructions of the local authorities, those responsible for tourist activities, a doctor or other health specialist, or signs warning of a danger or requiring certain behaviour; being in a state of alcoholic intoxication of more than 0.8 g/l of blood and/or drunkenness at the time of the accident; being in a similar state resulting from the consumption of drugs, medication or other hallucinogenic substances at the time of the claim; participation in a bet or challenge at the time of the claim.

An extreme sport is a particularly dangerous sporting activity that can expose you to serious injury or death in the event of an error or incident while practising it. Extreme sports can be practised in water, in the air or on land and often involves a high degree of risk, speed, height, natural challenges and physical commitment. Some sports are extreme by nature (e.g. sports involving jumping from a height) while others become extreme because of the circumstances in which they are practised (e.g. off-piste skiing or indoor climbing); Extreme sports include, but are not limited to: parachuting, paragliding, bungee jumping, base jumping, hang gliding, wingsuit jumping, outdoor climbing, kitesurfing, surfing, deep sea diving, ice diving, deep sea free diving, white water kayaking, mountaineering, canyoning, downhill mountain biking, off-piste skiing, Formula 1 and even motocross.

coverages.description: We offer you insurance cover for a temporary stay abroad if an insured event as defined in Article 10 occurs. If the insured event occurs, we will reimburse you for the expenses incurred for medically necessary treatment and generally provide the benefits specified in Article 11. The scope of your cover is determined by the contents of your insurance policy, the GTC and the legal provisions applicable to insurance contracts concluded in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

coverages.name: Recognised methods and medicines (Art. 11)
coverages.description: We provide benefits within the limits of the contract for examination and treatment methods and for medicines that are predominantly recognised as traditional medicine. In the latter case, however, we reserve the right to reduce our benefits to the amount that would have been paid if traditional methods or medicines had been used.

exclusions.description: Any natural person subject to an international economic or commercial sanction imposed on us and resulting from a resolution of the United Nations Security Council, a decision of the Council or Commission of the European Union, a legal or regulatory provision or a decision of the same nature, under international or national law and applicable in the territory of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg is excluded from cover.

exclusions.name: Stays in territories subject to a warning (Art. 9)
exclusions.description: Cover is also excluded for stays in territories for which the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, a competent ministry or a competent authority in one of the neighbouring countries of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg has issued a warning. In the event that you are on the territory of a country for which a warning has been issued, the insurance cover automatically expires at the end of a maximum period of fourteen (14) days following publication of such a warning.

obligations.name: Report the conditions of insurability
obligations.description: The existence of the conditions of insurability on the part of the policyholder and/or the insured person(s) must be reported to DKV Luxembourg S.A., at any time, on first request.
obligations.timing: At any time, on first request
obligations.sanction: Failing this, the insurance contract cannot take effect/will be null and void retroactively by application of the law, despite payment of the relevant premium.

obligations.name: Notify hospital treatment within three days
obligations.description: You must inform us of any hospital treatment within three days of undergoing treatment, either by telephone on (+352) 42 64 64 611 or by e-mail at assistance@dkv.lu.
obligations.timing: Within three days of undergoing treatment
obligations.sanction: Otherwise, we are not obliged to reimburse you and, if we receive the hospitalisation declaration later, we are obliged to grant the benefit only from the day we became aware of it.

obligations.name: Send original invoices to the statutory health insurance provider first
obligations.description: You must first send the original invoices, with proof of payment, to your statutory health insurance provider.

obligations.name: Send us copies with proof of statutory reimbursement
obligations.description: You must then send us copies of the same invoices, with proof of reimbursement from the compulsory health insurance, indicating your insurance number.

obligations.name: Send originals if the statutory scheme does not contribute
obligations.description: If the compulsory health insurance does not contribute to the costs, you must send us the original documents.
obligations.sanction: Otherwise we are not obliged to reimburse you.

obligations.name: Facilitate collection of information and provide supporting documents
obligations.description: Upon first request, you must also facilitate the collection of the information necessary for our intervention and provide us with all the supporting documents that we deem necessary to enable us to ascertain the insured event, to assess our obligation to provide a service and to determine the extent of our intervention. This provision exempts doctors from medical confidentiality, if necessary, within the framework of this article.

obligations.name: Send the official death certificate
obligations.description: In the event of a request for repatriation in the event of death, you must send us the official death certificate.

obligations.name: Be examined by a doctor appointed by us
obligations.description: At our request, you are required to be examined by a doctor appointed by us.

obligations.name: Responsibility for fulfilling the obligations
obligations.description: You are responsible for fulfilling the obligations set out in this article.

obligations.name: Consequences of breaching your obligations (Art. 15)
obligations.description: If you do not comply with the obligations set out in these GTC, the following sanctions apply: a) In the event of an intentional breach, we are exempt from the obligation to provide you with a service; b) In the event of a breach constituting gross negligence, we are only obliged to grant you the benefit if such a breach did not prevent us from ascertaining the insured event and/or from assessing our obligation to grant you the benefit, as well as its scope. The following breaches constitute gross negligence: failure to send us the supporting documents requested, despite two reminders; failure to appear for a second examination by our medical advisor, without justification received within two weeks of the request being sent. c) In other cases of breach, we may reduce our insurance benefits by the amount of the loss suffered as a result of the breach.
obligations.sanction: Intentional breach: exemption from the obligation to provide a service. Gross negligence: benefit only if the breach did not prevent ascertaining the event. Other cases: reduction by the amount of the loss suffered.

obligations.name: Notify any change of address (Art. 21)
obligations.description: You must notify us of any change of address. Otherwise, any communication sent to the last address known to us will be legally valid. Where applicable, the communication will take effect on the day it is notified to you.
obligations.sanction: Any communication sent to the last address known to us will be legally valid.

obligations.name: Assign rights against third parties (Art. 18)
obligations.description: If you are entitled to reimbursement of your loss from a third party, this right must be assigned to us in writing up to the amount of the reimbursement of costs as provided for in the insurance contract, without prejudice to legal subrogation.
obligations.sanction: If, without our agreement, you waive this right or any right useful for guaranteeing it, we are released from our obligation to provide a service to the extent that we could have requested reimbursement from the third party.

duration_and_cancellation.duration: The cover must be taken out for a minimum stay abroad per person of seven (7) days, even if the stay is shorter. The maximum duration of the cover is fifty-six (56) days (Art. 5). Your insurance cover takes effect on the date you specify when you take out the policy; the date is shown on your insurance policy. However, the cover will only take effect if: a) The insurance contract was validly concluded before your stay abroad, and; b) You have paid your premium, and; c) Your stay abroad has begun (Art. 6). Your cover ends on the day following the end date of cover stated in your insurance policy, or the last day of your stay abroad, or the day of your death (Art. 7).
methods: Claims should be sent to us in writing, either by post to DKV Luxembourg S.A. | 11-13, rue Jean Fischbach | L-3372 Leudelange, or by e-mail to info@dkv.lu (Art. 21)
special_rights: In the event of an illness or accident that makes your repatriation impossible on the expiry date of the cover, an extension of cover is granted to you, without any additional premium, for a period equal to the initial period, but with a maximum of twenty-eight (28) days (Art. 7)
Where the cover ends on the last day of your stay abroad, no refund of premium or extension of the duration of the cover will be granted (Art. 7)
In the event of your death, the cover continues to apply to any other insured persons indicated in the same insurance policy (Art. 7)

We may terminate your insurance contract, without notice, if you have received or attempted to receive insurance benefits through deception and/or fraudulent means. This provision does not affect any other right of cancellation provided for by law or regulation. The right of cancellation expires, if it has not been exercised, at the end of a period of one month from the date on which we became aware of the facts justifying the cancellation (Art. 20)

prescription_period.description: Any action arising from the insurance contract is time-barred on expiry of a period of three years, starting on the date of the event on which it is based. (Art. 19)

a) From zero to sixty-nine years (0 to 69 years): two euro (EUR 2.00) per person per day, including insurance tax

Costs generated in a foreign currency are converted into euro at the exchange rate of the day on which the insured event occurred. (Art. 16)

gaps: PORTEUR DU RISQUE : DKV Luxembourg S.A. Le contrat le dit lui-même par une définition, pas par un en-tête : « “We” (our):  DKV Luxembourg S.A; » (art. 1er). Le pronom ainsi défini est le sujet de tous les verbes de portage du contrat — « We offer you insurance cover » (art. 2), « we will reimburse you » (art. 2), « What benefits do we provide? » (art. 11), « We do not pay benefits for » (art. 12). L'adresse postale complète est imprimée à l'article 21 : « DKV Luxembourg S.A. | 11-13, rue Jean Fischbach | L-3372 Leudelange ». Ce document n'imprime PAS de numéro R.C.S. (contrairement aux CG BUSINESS TRAVEL allemandes et à la page de contact des CG maladie), ni la forme « Société Anonyme d'Assurances » pour DKV — cette forme n'y apparaît que pour les deux AUTRES sociétés du groupe.

PIÈGE INVERSE DE LA RAISON SOCIALE, À CONNAÎTRE POUR CE DOCUMENT : les seules dénominations portant une forme juridique développée sont « LA LUXEMBOURGEOISE Société Anonyme d'Assurances » et « LA LUXEMBOURGEOISE-VIE Société Anonyme d'Assurances ». Ni l'une ni l'autre ne porte le risque ici : elles sont citées uniquement comme les deux autres sociétés du groupe LALUX dont la qualité de client ouvre l'éligibilité. Une heuristique « nom + forme juridique » désignerait donc LA LUXEMBOURGEOISE — c'est exactement l'erreur que la spécification décrit, et elle aurait ici l'apparence d'une extraction réussie.

APPARTENANCE AU GROUPE, ÉNONCÉE PAR LE CONTRAT : « at least one of the three companies of the LALUX Group (LA LUXEMBOURGEOISE Société Anonyme d'Assurances, LA LUXEMBOURGEOISE-VIE Société Anonyme d'Assurances or DKV Luxembourg S.A.) ». DKV Luxembourg S.A. est donc, selon ses propres conditions générales, l'une des trois sociétés du groupe LALUX — la troisième aux côtés de la non-vie et de la vie. Fait relevé tel qu'imprimé.
